title: Test Simulation for Validation
pedagogical_goal: This simulation serves as a validation test to ensure the JSON specification generator produces syntactically correct, semantically rich, and visually dense simulations that adhere to all structural and mathematical requirements. It demonstrates the core principles of interactive parameter manipulation, real-time telemetry feedback, and layered visual composition without relying on domain-specific physics.

fundamental_laws: Parameter scaling follows linear transformation: output = input * scale_factor
Exponential decay governs medium opacity: opacity = base_opacity * Math.exp(-decay_rate * time_elapsed)
Particle motion follows harmonic oscillation: position = amplitude * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * frequency * time_elapsed + phase)

components.description: Layer 1: Structural background grid pattern with technical boundary benchmarks. Features a 20px spaced isometric grid in rgba(56,189,248,0.08) with major axes highlighted at 100px intervals. Includes coordinate system markers and scale indicators along edges.

components.description: Layer 2: Massive closed outer structural silhouette occupying 70% of viewport. Features a rounded rectangular frame with inward-tapering sides and reinforced corner gussets, simulating a test chamber or instrument housing. Path uses cubic Bezier curves for smooth contours.

Layer 3: Volumetric filled medium with dynamic linear gradient that shifts color and opacity based on scale_factor and decay_rate. Represents a reactive test medium whose properties change with input parameters, featuring animated glow pulses.
components.svg_content: <defs><linearGradient id='mediumGrad' x1='0%' y1='0%' x2='100%' y2='0%'><stop offset='0%' stop-color='rgba(56,189,248,0.6)' stop-opacity='{{medium_opacity}}'/><stop offset='100%' stop-color='rgba(244,63,94,0.4)' stop-opacity='{{medium_opacity}}'/></linearGradient><filter id='glowPulse'><feGaussianBlur stdDeviation='3' result='coloredBlur'/><feMerge><feMergeNode in='coloredBlur'/><feMergeNode in='SourceGraphic'/></feMerge></filter></defs><rect x='160' y='100' width='640' height='280' fill='url(#mediumGrad)' filter='url(#glowPulse)'/>

components.description: Layer 4: Dynamic particle system with count scaled by scale_factor. Particles follow Lissajous-style trajectories using derived formulas for x/y position, creating evolving geometric patterns that respond to frequency and amplitude controls.

Layer 5: In-situ instrumentation displaying live telemetry and governing equations. Features dynamic badges showing current parameter values, derived formulas, and real-time system status anchored within the visualization.

lifecycle_rules: Use React useRef for SVG/DOM node references
Use gsap.context() inside useEffect for flawless cleanup on re-render
MANDATE REAL KINETIC TRANSFORMS: Animate rotation for motors/rollers, translation for conveyors/drift, and scaleX/scaleY for morphological peristalsis/expansion
STRICT PROHIBITION on fake animations that merely toggle strokeDasharray on static lines
Smoothly tween reactive state transitions using gsap.to() with duration: 0.5
gsap_animation_directives.particle_animation: Each particle in #particleContainer should be animated with gsap.to({x: particle_x, y: particle_y, duration: 0.05, repeat: -1, yoyo: true, ease: 'sine.inOut'}), staggered by index * 0.02s. Update particle count dynamically based on {{particle_count}} variable.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Initial State
pedagogical_callouts.text: The system starts with default parameters: scale_factor=1.5, decay_rate=0.3, frequency=0.5Hz. Observe the medium's base color and the particle motion establishing the baseline behavior.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Parameter Interaction
pedagogical_callouts.text: Increasing scale_factor amplifies the output signal and increases particle count. Adjusting decay_rate controls how quickly the medium's opacity diminishes over time, demonstrating exponential decay dynamics.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Oscillatory Behavior
pedagogical_callouts.text: Modifying frequency and amplitude directly controls the particles' trajectory speed and radius. The Lissajous-like patterns emerge from the phase-shifted sine and cosine functions in the derived formulas.

pedagogical_callouts.title: System Equilibrium
pedagogical_callouts.text: At steady state, the telemetry metrics reflect the balanced interaction of all parameters. The system demonstrates how multiple physical processes (scaling, decay, oscillation) can be simultaneously controlled and observed in a unified framework.

technical_requirements.styling: Tailwind CSS utility classes or modern inline styles with dark glassmorphism
technical_requirements.no_broken_dependencies: All icons or helper components should be pure SVG or standard HTML to ensure instant zero-error execution in any preview environment
